name: Julian Kiverstein
abstract_title: Revisiting the DEUTS (Dynamic Entanglement plus Unique Temporal Signature) argument for Extended Consciousness in the light of Ecological Neuroscience
abstract: In 2009 Andy Clark, one of the main exponents of the theory of the extended mind, argued that the best arguments for the existence of extended consciousness make appeal to the circular causal dynamics of the whole embodied organism as it actively explores its environment. By extended consciousness I will refer to views that seek multiscale explanations of phenomenal consciousness that span the boundary that separates brain, body and world.
